races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Al Sayah
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter here and a key tactical factor — won over 24f on good ground recently and his visor keeps him focused, but a 53-day absence for Neil Mulholland's yard (0/5 in the last fortnight) is a mild concern and his record shows he can weakened late when things don't go to plan.

runners_data.name: Merrijig
runners_data.note: Jason Watson partners this eight-year-old who was placed over 16-17f on good ground in both his recent starts for John Berry, whose yard has landed 1/3 in the last 14 days — a genuine hold-up horse suited by this trip and going combination, with the blinkers on.

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has four winners from 34 runners over 14 days and Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lb — useful combination for a hold-up type who has struggled recently (three figures of 4-6-0 in form) but whose one win this season came over 16f on good ground, making the trip at least credible; needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Ben Case is 0/2 in the last fortnight and this mare has finished placed just twice in five runs without threatening a win — a confirmed hold-up operator whose true style sits deeper than the midfield position shown here, pushed there only because the rear of this field is crowded with closers; paddock headgear (p) worth noting.

runners_data.name: Oceanides
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles's four-year-old has form figures of 9-6-8-6-6 and has never won a race, with just one placed effort from six runs on similar going — a hold-up type by style but mapped to midfield simply due to the number of runners wanting the same ground at the back; difficult to make a case for improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Al Sayah is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, he will stride to the front and control fractions entirely on his own terms over 2m2f at Nottingham. Behind him, Merrijig, Simiyann, Regally Blonde, and Oceanides are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the race resolves into a straightforward leader-versus-closers contest with Al Sayah dictating every yard of the tempo. The field does hold more natural hold-up horses than the map can physically separate at the rear — Regally Blonde and Oceanides are true come-from-behind types who have been redistributed to midfield positions on the map simply because the rear is crowded, and in reality they are all likely to be racing in a tight, compacted bunch behind the leader. With Al Sayah able to set a measured, uncontested gallop over a stamina trip and no horse capable of forcing him to go faster than he chooses, this race shape strongly favours the patient hold-up profile that can sustain a late run — provided the leader does not steal an unassailable advantage with a well-judged front-running display.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Al Sayah Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah settles beautifully in front, controls a moderate gallop, and kicks decisively from the home turn before the hold-up pack can organise.
scenarios.body: Al Sayah sets fractions entirely to suit himself over the stamina trip, and with no rival willing or able to press him, he builds a winning cushion before the closers can wind up their challenges; his recent course-and-distance win at this sort of trip on good ground is directly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah sets a genuinely strong pace that leaves him vulnerable in the final quarter-mile, allowing the hold-up runners to close.
scenarios.body: The compacted group of hold-up horses — Merrijig most notably given his recent second over 16f on good ground and John Berry's trainer form — sweep past a weakening Al Sayah inside the final furlong; Merrijig's headgear and recent sharpness make him the likeliest beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah goes too hard early and blows up, leaving Simiyann or Merrijig to pick up the pieces in a messy finish.
scenarios.body: Al Sayah's visor and his record showing multiple out-of-the-frame finishes at longer distances hints at the possibility he overdoes it, creating a race in which the hold-up horses inherit a contest devoid of real pace judgement; Simiyann's Ian Williams yard is in decent form over 14 days and the 3lb claimer saves weight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and race-pace is so moderate that Regally Blonde or Oceanides — both natural hold-up types racing out of their preferred position — manage to find a clear run and rattle home.
scenarios.body: Regally Blonde has course form and the Harry Davies booking adds interest, but the pair's true style is deeper hold-up than the map shows and they are reliant on a perfectly-timed run from a compressed field; Oceanides remains a short-priced outsider with little recent evidence of competitive form at any distance.

watchPoints.text: Al Sayah's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the single biggest tactical factor — if he gets a soft lead and is allowed to dictate, his course-and-distance profile makes him dangerous despite the 53-day absence.

Merrijig is the hold-up horse with the strongest recent evidence at this trip and going combination — watch for Jason Watson to position him closest to the pace of the hold-up group so he can pounce if Al Sayah fades.

The entire field bar Al Sayah wants to come from off the pace — if Al Sayah sets a very steady gallop, the bunch will be tightly compressed turning for home and the winner could come from almost anywhere in the group on a fast-finishing run.

Regally Blonde and Oceanides are both natural come-from-behind types shown as midfielders on the map because the rear is congested — in practice expect them to be racing in a tight pack, and their redistribution means any scenario relying on them closing from truly far back is less likely to materialise.

Simiyann has the combination of a claimer saving 3lb and an in-form trainer — worth monitoring in the market to see if any confidence is shown, as his form figures alone do not recommend him strongly.

races.name: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)

runners_data.name: Black Missile
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's three-year-old has held-up form at 6f in good going but has found only one winner in five similar-ground runs; genuinely a closer by nature, this horse is pushed into a midfield map slot by the volume of hold-up types in the field, meaning it will need to produce something it has not yet shown in a race likely run at a moderate tempo.

runners_data.name: Rousham
runners_data.note: The most compelling profile among the redistribution group — Nigel Tinkler's gelding has won over 7f in good going and placed twice over 6f on good ground, giving it the best similar-going strike rate of the hold-up contingent; Faye McManoman rides and, although the horse's natural rear position will be hard to find in this field, its form credentials are genuine if the pace materialises.

runners_data.name: Liquid Cooled
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's gelding won over 6f on standard ground but that came at Carlisle and this represents a return after 82 days off; a natural hold-up horse who will struggle to find the strong pace it needs on a day when Slot is expected to set a comfortable tempo, and the limited similar-going exposure (one run) adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Slot
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's front-runner has consistency on its side — five runs at 5-6f including placed form on good ground — and Cam Hardie's job here is straightforward with no rival prepared to push from the gate; the style-fit tag acknowledges some role strain, but in practical terms Slot is simply the one horse who will actually be in front when the flag drops.

runners_data.name: Whizzy Dizzy
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old returns from 126 days off which demands a significant fitness question be answered first; a hold-up type by style who has placed twice over 5f on standard ground, the drop to turf on good going at 6f and the layoff make this one to monitor in the market rather than blindly trust.

runners_data.name: Robert Anstruther
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's gelding steps back to 6f having run a string of sevenths and fourths over 6-7f — the form is modest and the good-going strike rate (five runs, zero wins, one place) does not inspire confidence; by nature a hold-up horse, it will find itself racing closer to the pace than ideal given the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Night Mission
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's runner carries the highest OR in the field at 70 and has placed twice on good ground over 6f, but the unknown style tag is the critical variable — if Rawlinson sends him forward he becomes a genuine pace factor and race-shaper, and if he drops in he is a sit-and-watch hold-up type in a race that may not suit.

runners_data.name: Ballybunion
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old has placed twice over this exact course and distance on good going, giving it the most relevant course-form evidence in the field; a hold-up type who has been off 70 days, but the specific form ties to Nottingham at 6f on good ground are a legitimate angle if the race develops with any tempo at all.

races.paceDynamic: Slot is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 6f handicap and, with no genuine rival to push the pace from the outside, Cam Hardie should be able to dictate a sustainable gallop rather than a lung-bursting tempo. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Black Missile, Rousham, Liquid Cooled, Robert Anstruther and Ballybunion all want to come from off the pace — but with only one horse willing to lead, the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set things up for closers finishing out of the ground. Night Mission is an unknown quantity on style and may drift forward to apply some pressure, but Slot's position at the head of affairs looks secure. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or make a forward move from a handy position turning in, rather than true hold-up horses that need a strong pace to close into — this field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate, and those redistributed horses (Rousham, Black Missile, Robert Anstruther, Liquid Cooled) are unlikely to secure their natural rear-of-field positions, meaning they must race out of role and their finishing kick will be blunted by a moderate pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slot Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Slot bowls along at a comfortable tempo and faces no serious pressure from the front.
scenarios.body: Slot dictates from the gate with Cam Hardie setting a pace entirely on his own terms, denying closers the strong gallop they need; the field fans out in the straight but the hold-up horses lack the raw closing velocity to peg back a horse conserving energy in front. Horses with the ability to track close to the pace without expending excess energy in the first half of the race are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Night Mission Presses, Gets There
scenarios.trigger: If Night Mission travels prominently, applies pressure to Slot through the middle and hits the front inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Night Mission's unknown style tag leaves open the possibility he drifts closer than expected and uses his higher OR rating to grind past a front-runner carrying more weight; a race run at a pressured but not extreme tempo would suit a horse with proven placed form over this course and distance combination. The moderate closing opportunity also allows Rousham — who managed to win over this exact trip in good going — to finish strongly if he can navigate the likely traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Sprint Through
scenarios.trigger: If Night Mission or another runner kicks up early and the tempo rises sharply enough to string the field out.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong pace would reverse the dominant shape, turning the race into a test of finishing speed and stamina for the hold-up brigade; Rousham has winning form over 6f in good going, and Ballybunion has twice placed over this course and distance in similar conditions, making both viable beneficiaries of a true end-to-end gallop. The probability is discounted because the hold-up horses are not in their natural positions and the single confirmed pace-setter makes a truly strong pace unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Midfield Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches early, traffic develops and the race is effectively decided by a sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: In a slow-run race that suddenly accelerates, horses with tactical speed and good recent form rather than outright hold-up ability will find themselves perfectly placed; Whizzy Dizzy has consistent placed form on standard ground and Ballybunion has twice gone close at this level, both capable of capitalising on a messy, compressed finish. This scenario remains a low-probability outlier because Slot's lead is unlikely to be so easily swallowed up this quickly.

watchPoints.text: Slot — if Cam Hardie is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and regulate the gallop entirely to his own satisfaction, the race is effectively being run to suit this horse from the moment the stalls open.

Night Mission — Alistair Rawlinson's decision on where to position this horse in the early stages is the single biggest tactical unknown; if Night Mission goes forward and applies pressure, the whole race shape changes from a solo leader scenario to a two-horse duel.

Rousham — watch the market for Nigel Tinkler's runner, whose good-going form over this trip is the most credible in the hold-up group; if punters identify it as the closest to a legitimate closer with a genuine winning run in similar conditions, any drift or support will be informative.

Whizzy Dizzy — 126 days off is a significant layoff for a three-year-old with no win from six starts; Clive Cox does have a 4/25 14-day trainer strike rate suggesting horses are tuned up, but the fitness angle is worth tracking in the paddock.

Liquid Cooled — 82 days since last run and only one career start on good going; Andrew Mullen is an experienced claimer but the combination of a lengthy absence and the most limited similar-conditions form in the field makes this horse one to identify visually before committing to any view.

races.name: PKF Wish Race Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's hold-up horse arrives on a 17-day break with a recent course win over 6f on good ground to his name (3rd last time, winner before that), and his sim-going record of 3 runs producing 1 win and 2 places is the most solid in the field; he will need a prominent stalker to deliver off a slow pace here.

runners_data.name: Baileys Ontherocks
runners_data.note: Jason Watson takes the ride for the Carroll yard fresh off a 10-day break; his natural inclination is to race from the rear but the crowded hold-up contingent means he is unlikely to get fully settled, and a poor sim-going record of zero wins from 12 on similar ground is a further dampener.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this 3-year-old who recorded a wide-margin 6f win on good ground but whose recent form string of 557177 tells a story of inconsistency; the 18-day break is not a concern, and the true hold-up style could work if a strong pace materialises, but that looks unlikely here.

runners_data.name: Jackie Brown
runners_data.note: The one genuine front-runner in the race, Adrian Wintle's six-year-old carries a tongue-tie and goes on good ground with 7 sim-going runs in the bank; the sole pace-setter means he faces zero pressure early, and his recent 3rd at 6f on good was encouraging — the shorter 5f trip is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Benoit de la Sayette takes over on a 44-day layoff for this 4-year-old who stays on from hold-up; the lengthy break is the primary concern, and although naturally a closer, he will be shuffled into a midfield role in a race with too many horses wanting the same ground late, blunting his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Sir Benedict
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen's mount has placed twice from five runs on similar going and showed up well at 5f at Goodwood last time; at 8 years old he races fresh off 29 days and his hold-up style, while natural, benefits more than most from any pace injection — he remains a player if the leader weakens.

runners_data.name: Antiphon
runners_data.note: A well-documented finisher who fades in the closing stages according to the data flag, Callum Hutchinson inherits a horse whose last two runs both ended in late retreat; placed three times on good or good-soft over 6f, but dropping to 5f with a pattern of finishing runs short of the line is a genuine concern, not just a positional one.

runners_data.name: Captain Kinsella
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's 4-year-old returns from a long 123-day absence and has failed to win or place in 15 sampled runs on this type of going; Rhys Clutterbuck has a mountain to climb with a horse that races exclusively on Standart ground in his history and meets this surface for the first time today in competitive shape.

runners_data.name: Desert Master
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners Antony Brittain's 5-year-old who has shown genuine ability on good ground — two seconds from four sampled good-ground runs over 5-6f — and wears a visor to sharpen focus; though pushed out of his natural rear position by the crowded hold-up market, his recent 6-furlong good-ground form is the most convincing late-closer profile in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Jackie Brown is the sole confirmed front-runner and should dictate from the front in an uncontested manner, setting a sustainable gallop over five furlongs on good ground at Nottingham. With no natural challenger willing or able to take Jackie Brown on for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be franctic, which typically compresses the finish and keeps front-runners and prominent racers in their comfort zone throughout. The bulk of this field — Baileys Ontherocks, Antiphon, Captain Kinsella, Desert Master, and Rinky Tinky Tinky — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for the rear to accommodate them all; in practice, several will find themselves closer to the pace than their natural style dictates, muddying their individual prospects. This race shape — a single uncontested leader, a moderate gallop, and a pack of hold-up horses unable to fully settle — strongly favours Jackie Brown and any horse able to track closely in the prominent-to-midfield bracket, as late closers will face a compressed finish with diminishing ground to make up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackie Brown Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown secures an uncontested lead and the pace remains controlled, allowing the front-runner to husband enough energy to hold on.
scenarios.body: Jackie Brown dictates every yard from the front with no challenger for the lead, setting a tempo that never truly tests her stamina reserves over five furlongs; the moderate pace means the hold-up brigade face a wall of horses at the death with too little ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent racer stalks Jackie Brown close enough to pounce inside the final furlong as the leader's effort flattens out.
scenarios.body: Washington Heir or Sir Benedict, tracking just off the pace, benefits from the controlled tempo and produces a timely challenge in the closing stages without having to make up significant ground; the good going suits a horse with a clean recent run in similar conditions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm a Flat Finale
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens markedly in the middle part of the race and Jackie Brown ties up inside the final furlong, opening a gap for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Desert Master or Ganthorpe, both carrying recent good-ground form at this trip, arrive late with momentum if the field concertinas at the two-furlong pole; this scenario is constrained by the reality that most of the true closers are pushed out of their natural position and will not be fully settled.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If several runners dispute early positions with Jackie Brown, creating an unsettled tempo that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Horses redistributed from their natural hold-up roles bump into each other for midfield berths, creating interference and uneven fractions that make the race unpredictable; a horse like Antiphon or Captain Kinsella, finally able to find daylight, could sneak into the frame but the probability is low given the field's lack of genuine pace threat to Jackie Brown.

watchPoints.text: Jackie Brown sets every fraction unchallenged — if she gets a completely uncontested lead and the early sectionals are slow, hold-up horses including Desert Master and Ganthorpe will simply have too little time to close on the short 5f trip.

Captain Kinsella returns from 123 days off with zero wins or places on this type of going — watch for signs of ring-rustiness or greenness in the early stages that could cause interference among the crowded midfield group.

Antiphon carries a data flag for fading in the finish, and with the race likely to produce a compressed finale rather than an end-to-end gallop, any horse drawn near Antiphon risks being hampered if he weakens sharply inside the final furlong.

Baileys Ontherocks and Rinky Tinky Tinky are both natural hold-up horses forced into midfield — watch how quickly they settle in the first furlong, as restlessness or over-racing could compromise both their own chances and those of horses around them.

Washington Heir's jockey Jack Doughty must decide early whether to push up to track Jackie Brown or accept a hold-up role — the tactical call in the first half-furlong will significantly shape whether Washington Heir is competitive or left with an impossible task on a short course.

races.name: Arthur Johnson & Sons Wish Race "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Goldie Trickett
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer for Jane Chapple-Hyam with decent Good-ground form, returning after a 34-day break at her preferred surface; her sim-going record of just 3 runs limits the sample, but she has placed once at the trip and holds the cleanest hold-up credentials in the field.

runners_data.name: Token Love
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's 4-year-old returns after 79 days off wearing headgear for the first time (t), and while the layoff is a mild flag, her one placing on similar ground came at 10f suggesting the trip suits; a natural closer who will need the race to develop a strong late pace to land her challenge.

runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: The veteran 10-year-old is Adrian Wintle's most active runner over the past 14 days (3/7), and while his Good-ground record over the trip is extensive, he is at heart a hold-up horse shifted into midfield on the map — his best chance comes if the sprint finish suits his residual acceleration rather than a true tactical race.|

runners_data.name: Finally Escaped
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 4-year-old has shown headgear (ht) and carries the lightest qualifying weight among the older runners, but a 84-day absence and a form string of five consecutive defeats raises fitness doubts; placed just twice in six starts and, though mapped to midfield, his natural instinct is to race from the rear.

runners_data.name: Brouhaha
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3-year-old is the freshest horse in the race at just 16 days since last run, but three consecutive sixth-place finishes on Good ground paint a bleak form picture; the age and weight allowance are pluses, though his racing pattern instinctively drifts back regardless of the map position shown.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland sends this 3-year-old up from the south after 99 days off — the longest layoff in the field — with a warning flag for fading in finishes and a form string of consecutive placings in the 8th-to-10th range; the step up to 1m2f is potentially interesting but the fade tendency makes him a concern in any shape that requires a strong closing effort.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f Nottingham contest faces a genuine tactical vacuum — somebody will have to lead, but nobody wants the job. The race is likely to be run at a crawl early before compressing into a sprint finish from the home turn, favouring whoever can produce the sharpest late acceleration. Goldie Trickett and Token Love, as the two horses with the cleanest hold-up credentials not tagged as redistributed, are best positioned to exploit a muddling pace from the rear. The redistributed runners — Revich, Finally Escaped, Brouhaha, and Nicolai — are all genuine hold-up types shuffled into the midfield slots on the map; in a race this slow-run, they are unlikely to secure any meaningful positional advantage, and the shape overwhelmingly favours horses with a clean late kick over those forced to race out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crawl Then Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses from the gate and the race turns into a dash from two furlongs out
scenarios.body: With no natural leader, the field idles in the first mile before a fierce sprint develops on the home turn, compressing the entire field into a tight bunch; horses with the sharpest acceleration and lightest weight benefit most from the neutralised early gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one reluctant front-runner gets nudged forward and sets a steady but uncontested pace
scenarios.body: A single horse — likely pushed forward from the jockeys' stand — controls fractions alone without pressure, potentially stealing first run on the field turning in; a prominent horse that travels well and has tactical pace to quicken wins this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Opens Race
scenarios.trigger: If two or more horses are pushed forward early and a genuine pace develops
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop stretches the field and tests stamina over the 1m2f trip, exposing the lower-rated closers who lack the staying power to reel in a front-runner who has conserved energy; a horse with a blend of stamina and class takes advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Seizes Momentum
scenarios.trigger: If a lesser-fancied runner secures a perfect box-seat position and times a run to perfection
scenarios.body: Brouhaha or Nicolai, typically at the rear but finding an uncontested berth just off the pace, produces a smooth move widest of all entering the straight; a clean passage and a fresh pair of legs can compensate for lack of form in a race run below full gallop.

watchPoints.text: Goldie Trickett and Token Love are both genuine hold-up horses in a race with zero natural pace — watch whether Callum Hutchinson or Aiden Brookes instinctively drop their mounts to the back together, creating a genuine vacuum that hands a free lead to a reluctant front-runner.

Revich's jockey Harry Davies may be forced to take up a more prominent position than the horse likes in the absence of any natural pace-setter — watch the opening two furlongs to see whether he gets shuffled forward against his instincts.

Token Love's first-time headgear (t) combined with a 79-day absence is a dual unknown; watch the market moves and paddock demeanour for signs that Micky Hammond has her cherry-ripe or that the gear switch changes her racing behaviour.

Nicolai is flagged as a horse that fades in finishes and arrives after 99 days off — in a sprint finish scenario, watch whether Cam Hardie positions him boldly to avoid being caught flat-footed by the late charge.

The going is listed as unknown throughout the card at Nottingham — watch the early races for any ground description updates from jockeys or the clerk of the course, as any significant deviation from Good could reshuffle the form claims across this field.
